Chapter 10: Living with Openness, Joy, and Wonder.
As you keep going on your meditation journey, something pretty special starts to show up. It's this gentle sense of openness... a quiet joy, and a real wonder at just being alive. But here's the thing—it's not that quick burst of happiness when you get exactly what you want. No, it's deeper than that. It's the kind of contentment that sticks around, even when life isn’t perfect.
Imagine taking a walk through your own neighborhood, maybe a place you’ve seen a hundred times before. Suddenly, you start to notice things you’ve always missed—the way sunlight dances through the leaves, the chorus of birds, or the laughter of kids chasing each other down the block. There’s this feeling of wonder, a quiet gratitude for all those little miracles that fill up everyday life. Maybe you find yourself smiling, not because everything’s going right, but because you’re finally awake to the beauty that’s always been there.
Most of us, let’s be honest, are usually racing from one thing to the next, always thinking about what’s missing or what’s coming up. But meditation offers another way. It invites you to slow down, to really pay attention, and to savor what’s here, right now. You discover that joy isn’t hiding in some big, extraordinary moment. It’s right there in the small stuff—a meal shared with someone you love, a thoughtful word, or a peaceful evening at home.
Let me share a quick story. Picture someone who’s spent years chasing after happiness, always striving for something more. And then, one day, they realize happiness isn’t something you achieve—it’s something you notice. The endless search quiets down, and suddenly, there’s a sense of ease. They find themselves laughing more, stressing less, and feeling more at home in the world.
Living with openness means being willing to feel it all—the sweet moments, the tough ones, the things you understand, and the mysteries that make you pause. It’s about letting go of those tight expectations, allowing each moment to show up exactly as it is. It’s trusting your heart’s wisdom, and being open to surprise.
Over time, this way of living just becomes part of who you are. You stop trying to control everything, and instead, you’re more willing to receive whatever comes your way. There’s a new lightness, a freedom that comes from letting go. And right at the center of it all, there’s this steady, quiet joy—a deep sense that, even with all its ups and downs, life is a gift.
